Keywords: Early House of Habsburg Red Lion
RagShortTexts: From Habichtsburg Castle in Swiss Aargau, the House of Habsburg steadily accumulated Alpine.

Variants.Content: Habichtsburg ('Hawk's Castle') in Swiss Aargau gave the Habsburgs their name, and they bore a crowned red lion rampant on gold. Count Rudolf I expanded patrimonial estates across Swabia and the Aargau through marriage contracts, clientage to bishops, and the suppression of robber knights. Rudolf kept his lands together while the Empire had no emperor, using the Great Interregnum to build alliances with towns and bishops. Those ties let his family outmatch the older princes on the Upper Rhine. His steady accumulation of land made the Habsburg name a power to reckon with long before he took the crown.

Rhenish electors saw Rudolf as an unthreatening minor count, and they underestimated the military networks he was quietly building. Each castle he secured and each town he drew into his service gave him more knights for a future bid. Letters between his chancery and the electoral courts were polite, and the electors learned too late how much support he had gathered.
Habsburg bailiffs enforce predictable manorial tithes without extortion. Count Rudolf personally leads cavalry to hang highwaymen preying on rustic trade routes.
